label: rem:trace-ratio-interpretation
title: Trace ratio computational results and the half-life formula
html:
Remark. Trace ratio computational results and the half-life formula

Computational results. The trace ratio \hat{V}^{\mathrm{par}} / \hat{V}^{\mathrm{dau}} at each affected generator is tabulated for all six verification nuclei in Table: Trace ratio per affected generator.

The trace ratio grows with p (the number of affected generators), reflecting the increasing number of crossings that change type. The squared ratio |\mathcal{M}_q|^2 spans 10 orders of magnitude. The observed variation in nuclear matrix elements is smaller: \log ft from 3 to 9 corresponds to |M|^2 spanning \sim 10^6. The two are the same kind of quantity and the model range brackets the observed one, but it over-spans it by about four orders of magnitude, so this is a consistency-of-scale remark and not a quantitative match.

The growth of the ratio with p means heavier nuclei have larger topological matrix elements, which drives faster decay rates. This aligns with the observation that allowed beta transitions in heavy nuclei tend to have shorter half-lives (smaller \log ft) than those in light nuclei.

The half-life formula (final form). We combine the trace ratio with the phase space integral:

  t_{1/2}
  = 
  \frac{\ln 2 \cdot 2N_v^4}{243\mathfrak{E}_{\times} \cdot \mu_0}
   \cdot 
  \frac{1}{[2]_q  \cdot  s^2}
   \cdot 
  \frac{1}{f(Z_d, Q)}
   \cdot 
  \prod_{i=0}^{p}
  \left|
    \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{dau}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{par}}}
  \right|^2

Here s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2} is the Skein amplitude, \mathfrak{E}_{\times} = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) is the crossing energy, \mu_0 is the single dimensional scale, and N_v is the effective crossing count of the weak scale (v = N_v\mathfrak{E}_{\times}\mu_0). The function f(Z_d, Q) is the Coulomb-corrected phase space integral (Skein-Coulomb enhancement). The prefactor replaces the standard-physics combination G_F^2m_e^5/(2\pi^3) (hadron half-life). The product of volume ratios provides the topological part of |\mathcal{M}_q|^2.
